how_to_read_this: These are the places where the PINNED CONTROL violates the specification.
Each record keeps its test at full strength. The test still runs and still
asserts. Matching it here only accounts for the failure, so the suite is
green overall while continuing to assert the behaviour.
A SECOND deviation is not covered by these records and breaks the green.
A deviation that changes shape breaks the green. A deviation that gets
fixed upstream breaks the green, so the record must be removed on purpose
Nothing in this file may be a spec ambiguity. If the spec permits the
behaviour then the TEST is too strict and the test must be fixed instead.

deviations.clause: SPEC 5.6.1 Timestamps: 'Timezone: UTC (denoted by Z suffix)' and 'Timestamps MUST NOT include timezone offsets other than Z (all times are UTC).'
deviations.observed_bytes: "timestamp": "2026-08-08T16:35:07.065632-07:00" in TaskStatus.timestamp on the response to POST /message:send
deviations.judgement: Real defect in a2a-go v2.4.0. It serialises task status timestamps in the host's local zone instead of UTC. Confirmed as a control defect and not a misreading of the spec by the second control, a2a-python 1.1.2, which emits '2026-08-08T23:23:34.117771Z' correctly for the same field. Note this defect is invisible to anyone testing on a UTC host, which is most CI, so it would not have been found by a suite that only ran in CI.
deviations.impact_if_a_subject_did_this: Any client sorting or comparing task times across agents in different regions orders them wrongly, and any client parsing strictly for a trailing Z rejects the response outright.

deviations.clause: SPEC 3.6.2 Server Responsibilities: 'Agents MUST process requests using the semantics of the requested A2A-Version (matching Major.Minor). If the version is not supported by the interface, agents MUST return a VersionNotSupportedError.'
deviations.evidence: a version it does not declare support for
deviations.observed_bytes: POST /message:send with header 'A2A-Version: 0.5' against a card declaring only protocolVersion 1.0 returns HTTP 200 and a completed task, instead of VersionNotSupportedError (SPEC 5.4 maps that to HTTP 400 / JSON-RPC -32009).
deviations.judgement: Real defect in a2a-go v2.4.0. It ignores the A2A-Version header entirely rather than negotiating on it. Confirmed as a control defect by the second control, a2a-python 1.1.2, which rejects the same request. The spec is unusually explicit here, with a worked example in SPEC 6.4, so there is no ambiguity to hide behind.
deviations.impact_if_a_subject_did_this: A client pinned to a newer protocol version is silently served older semantics and loses functionality with no error anywhere, which is exactly the silent-downgrade failure SPEC 3.6.3 warns about.

deviations.clause: SPEC 3.3.2 Error Handling, Validation Errors: 'Servers MUST validate all input parameters before processing.' The mapped error is HTTP 400 / JSON-RPC -32602, not a server fault.
deviations.observed_bytes: POST /message:send with body {"message":{"messageId":"m9","role":"ROLE_USER","parts":[null]}} returns HTTP 500 with message 'event producer panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference'. On the JSON-RPC binding the same input returns JSON-RPC error -32603 inside an HTTP 200. An earlier run of the same input produced 'gob: encodeArray: nil element', so more than one code path is reachable.
deviations.judgement: Real defect in a2a-go v2.4.0, and the most serious finding in this battery: a null element inside the parts array reaches a nil dereference, so a 60-byte well-formed JSON document panics a goroutine in an unauthenticated request path. Confirmed as a control defect by the second control, a2a-python 1.1.2, which rejects the same input cleanly. Worth reporting upstream.
deviations.impact_if_a_subject_did_this: An unauthenticated remote crash. Any peer, hostile or merely buggy, can fault the agent at will.
